Show that the sequence $\\left(f_{n}\\right)$ does not converge uniformly.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "topology", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "target": {"node_id": "n2", "version": 2}, "target_node": {"text": "The sequence $\\left(f_n\\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\\varepsilon<1$ and $N \\in \\mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\\left(f_N(x), f(x)\\right)=\\varepsilon$.", "claim": "Claims nonuniform convergence by choosing, for each positive integer $N$ and $0<\\varepsilon<1$, the point $x=\\varepsilon^{1/N}$. The calculation requires the unstated pointwise limit $f(x)=0$ for $x<1$; fixing one such $\\varepsilon$, for example $1/2$, would then match the negation of uniform convergence.", "scope": [], "depends_on": ["n2_bridge_limit"]}, "closed_predecessors": [{"node_id": "n2_bridge_limit", "version": 1, "claim": "Establishes the pointwise limit and shows that any possible uniform limit must be this function.", "text": "For every $x\\in[0,1)$, $x^n\\to0$, while $f_n(1)=1$ for every $n$. Thus $(f_n)$ converges pointwise to the function $f$ defined by $f(x)=0$ for $x<1$ and $f(1)=1$. Any uniform limit would also be a pointwise limit, so it would necessarily equal this $f$.", "scope": [], "depends_on": []}], "counterexample_search": true, "rule_candidates": [{"id": "grp_normal_quotient", "name": "Quotient group criterion", "statement": "If N is a normal subgroup of G, then the set of left cosets G/N forms a group under (aN)(bN) = abN.", "conditions": ["N is a subgroup of G", "N is normal in G"], "conclusion": "G/N is a group and coset multiplication is well-defined.", "rule_digest": "f6d458aa2e7463efeea7a535cdbe0f0f7930259cfe7f845b5350ec03454da876", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_first_iso", "name": "First isomorphism theorem for groups", "statement": "If phi: G -> H is a group homomorphism, then G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "conditions": ["phi is a group homomorphism", "ker(phi) is the kernel of phi"], "conclusion": "G/ker(phi) is isomorphic to im(phi).", "rule_digest": "335c687d26f64e41584f1b8bc575aec9d78223b01c4821bf0056bf8533de0c19", "applicability": "unchecked"}, {"id": "grp_lagrange", "name": "Lagrange theorem", "statement": "If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup of G, then |H| divides |G|.", "conditions": ["G is finite", "H is a subgroup of G"], "conclusion": "|H| divides |G|.", "rule_digest": "361a6b53eb7c1cb71cc90836aab9022d76163052528c559907341ebabe9bf547", "applicability": "unchecked"}]}
